claims.text: Kanban manages work as a continuous flow through the stages of a board, with no fixed-length sprint and no sprint goal; items are pulled into the next column when capacity frees up.
claims.source_hint: glossary kanban; The Kanban Guide (2020): flow, pull; docs/team/kanban-board-example.md

claims.text: The Scrum Guide 2020 defines a fixed-length Sprint with a Sprint Goal and does not prescribe any board or how the Sprint Backlog is visualised.
claims.source_hint: Scrum Guide 2020: The Sprint, Sprint Goal, Sprint Backlog

claims.text: docs/team/kanban-board-example.md@stage-1 lines 8-12 show four columns (Việc cần làm, Đang làm (giới hạn 2), Chờ review (giới hạn 2), Xong) with the listed items and developers; lines 24-28 explain that the support team (Dev 1, Dev 2) has no sprint and the feature team (Dev 3, Dev 4) keeps sprints.
In Sprint 14, 'Ngừng gửi thông báo cho đơn đã hủy' did not finish and moved to the next sprint.
Teams usually start a new sprint board with each sprint's backlog, so it shows one sprint's slice; many teams combine Scrum's roles and events with a Kanban-style board.
